core_findings: Coconut Creek remains a real incorporated municipal police target with an active city-run police department. The official city police page describes the Coconut Creek Police Department as a full-service, fully accredited agency, and the official accreditation page says the department has an authorized strength of 119 police officers and 44 civilian members serving approximately 60,000 residents.

The city's official police history page rejects any contract-policing or county-replacement interpretation. It says Coconut Creek established its own police force in 1969 and formally re-established the separate Coconut Creek Police Department on September 12, 2002.

FDLE's official 2020 County and Municipal Offense Report publishes Coconut Creek Police Department as a distinct Broward municipal row with population 58,803 and total index crime 750. FDLE's 2021 report retains Coconut Creek Police Department with population 57,871 but blanks every offense field.

FDLE's official incident-based reporting page says Florida's public FIBRS offense workbook covers the 2021-2024 and 2025 Q2 reporting cycles. Inspection of that workbook finds no Coconut Creek row in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, or 2025 Q2 even though other Broward agencies do appear.

The official FBI CDE 2024 roster snapshot in the repo still lists FL0061100 as Coconut Creek Police Department with agency type City, but marks is_nibrs false and provides no nibrs_start_date. That preserves the agency identity while confirming there is no usable 2024 NIBRS surface.

Repo artifacts align with a post-2020 continuity failure rather than target invalidity. The live crosswalk routes FL0061100 exclusively to Coconut Creek city; repo observations contain nonzero SRS annual totals in 2018-2020 and then zero-valued annual SRS placeholders in 2021-2024; and 2024 Coconut Creek controls are fully fill-backed with zero reported support.

governance_structure.important_interpretation: Coconut Creek is a valid municipal control object. There is no evidence that Broward County Sheriff's Office, county remainder, or a contract-policing arrangement displaced the city's own police function.

The same workbook does include other Broward agencies such as Miramar in 2021; Coral Springs, Davie, Miramar, Seminole Police Department, and Town of Southwest Ranches in 2022; Coral Springs, Davie, Fort Lauderdale, Miramar, and Town of Southwest Ranches in 2023; and Coral Springs, Davie, Fort Lauderdale, Hillsboro Beach, Miramar, Pembroke Pines, and Seminole Police Department in 2024.
fdle_post_srs_fibrs_publication_check.interpretation: The public Florida incident-based workbook is not missing Broward generally; it is missing Coconut Creek specifically.

why: Coconut Creek has an active city police department in current official city materials.
FDLE's official county-and-municipal reports publish Coconut Creek as a distinct municipal reporting row in 2020 and retain the row in 2021.
The official FBI CDE roster still recognizes FL0061100 as a City agency even though it marks the agency non-NIBRS in 2024.
The repo crosswalk from FL0061100 to Coconut Creek city is exclusive and consistent with those official identity surfaces.
likely_explanation_for_current_all_fill_: Coconut Creek remained a real city-police reporting identity through the end of the SRS publication lane and appears as a retained blank row in FDLE's 2021 annual county-and-municipal report.

That identity did not carry into a usable public post-2020 incident-based reporting surface: the FBI's 2024 roster marks FL0061100 non-NIBRS and FDLE's public FIBRS workbook omits Coconut Creek entirely.
The repo therefore falls back from real 2018-2020 annual support to zero-valued placeholders in 2021-2024 and fully fill-backed 2024 municipal controls.

The public FDLE FIBRS workbook contains no Coconut Creek row, and the official FBI 2024 roster marks the agency non-NIBRS.

recommended_handling: Retain Coconut Creek city as a standalone municipal control row.
Do not reroute Coconut Creek to Broward Sheriff's Office, county remainder, or any contract-policing treatment.
Treat the current all-fill state as a post-2020 reporting continuity failure on FL0061100 rather than contract policing, county replacement, or target invalidity.
Use FDLE's county-and-municipal offense reports as the official statewide support surface through 2020 and treat the retained blank 2021 row as transition evidence.
If production requires observed counts after 2020, recover them through direct city records or a direct agency-level state or federal extract rather than deleting the municipal target.

open_questions: The keep-versus-drop decision is closed. The remaining implementation blocker is that no reviewed official public annual offense table exposes Coconut Creek counts for 2021-2024; recovery would require direct city records or a direct FDLE/FBI agency extract keyed to FL0061100.
